title: Canonical induced linearization on immersion Tor
statement: Let $G$ act on schemes $Y,W$ over a scheme $S$ and let $i:W\to Y$ be equivariant, with action-groupoid presentations and coherent linearized modules as in [def-sfb-equivariant-coherent-gzero]. Use the recorded module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], with their recorded derived pullback $Lf^*$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. For each action or projection $f$, an exact-pullback model consists of additivity, preservation of finite limits and finite colimits for $f^*$, and an isomorphism from $Lf^*$ to the induced exact derived functor, normalized to its original recorded localization counit. For a coherent linearized $M$ on $Y$, define $T_q(M)=H^{-q}(Li^*(M[0]))$ on $W$ for $q\geq0$; this is derived extension of scalars by $\mathcal O_W$. Write $j=\mathrm{id}_G\times i$. The equivariant squares $a_Wi=ja_Y$ and $p_Wi=jp_Y$, the counit-normalized composition isomorphisms [lem-pc-recorded-pullback-composition], the given $a_Y^*M\simeq p_Y^*M$, and the exact-pullback comparisons on degree-zero objects define the derived comparison $La_W^*Li^*M[0]\simeq Lp_W^*Li^*M[0]$. Taking $H^{-q}$ and the normalized exact-pullback cohomology comparisons defines $a_W^*T_q(M)\simeq p_W^*T_q(M)$. A coherent Tor realization is a coherent linearized module on $W$ with an underlying isomorphism to this actual $T_q(M)$ intertwining that comparison. No existence or vanishing theorem is part of this definition.
